LESSON: WRITING 8.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING: SELF-ASSESSMENT

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.5: Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to assess writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions
2. write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion
3. appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 8.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING: SELF-ASSESSMENT
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 8.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING: SELF-ASSESSMENT
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions

What this means
In this part you learn to identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion

What this means
In this part you learn to write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment to a partner. (skill: write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions.
3. Practise this skill: write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to assess writing?
2. How can one improve their composition writing skills?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions.
5. Be able to: write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
